answer: Each challenge commits to a future drand quicknet round, then derives its nonce from that round’s threshold-BLS beacon pulse; before publication, no operator can know the nonce or precompute valid responses. Commit-reveal binds each response to the pulse and task, so cached work cannot be replayed across identities. A marble, tide, or vertex task is equally unpredictable; Sybil resistance comes from requiring fresh, verifiable work after the pulse, not from beacon randomness alone.
